title: Returning to playing after seven months
summary: Freeman did not play for seven months, then felt no pain at Art Hodes's Chicago show; he mentions lung puncture and catching colds in England.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Well, I was very lucky. I had no ill effects from it. The first show I did, I didn't do anything for seven months, and Art Hodes called me from Chicago -- he had that wonderful show, I think it was called Blues Alley. And he asked me if I'd come out. And the doctor said now you might feel some pain when you start to play again, because the expansion and all, but there was nothing. No pain, it was marvelous and I played that first thing and that started me all over again.
You mean you actually hadn't blown, you hadn't played at all.
I hadn't played in seven months. I stayed away from it to let the thing heal.
Stan and I were just talking about
that rib business. You didn't run any risk of pneumonia, then, Bud. You had to be pretty careful.

I could easily have got that and there was a slight puncture of one of the lungs, but never had any -- but I do catch, as much as I love living in England, I do catch colds here, which I have never caught, because I have been taking Vitamin C for about 20 years and Vitamin E, but I do catch colds here, catch chills.
